summary: New sense 4: (vor Gericht) verurteilen, gegen jemanden entscheiden
rationale: The opposing bribes ask adjudicators to rule against the other litigant. Two parallel clauses in one episode; legal meaning is supported by that setting, though detention remains an editorial question.

summary: New sense 6: (Fahrzeuge, Reittiere, Räume) mieten, buchen
rationale: Merge transport/premises procurement; explicit b-price at 217 and 241 establishes rental, distinct from employment of people in round-1 I.2. Contractual terms of the hall are less explicit.

rationale: ḥšəwle precedes the total and šqile meni separately gives actual payment: an amount construction, not taking money.

summary: New sense 8: (von Zaubersprüchen) wirken, anschlagen
rationale: məskiwo/lə məskiwo refer back to səḥərat and written charms: efficacy, not possessing magical powers. Two tokens, one passage only.

summary: New sense 9: (mit ʕam-) sich jemandem anschließen, zu jemandem halten

data.gloss: (mit ʕam-) sich jemandem anschließen, zu jemandem halten

rationale: ṭray mənayye followed by lə məskət aʕmayye prohibits association, not capture; one clear attestation.

summary: New sense 10: (Personen) unterstützen, sich für jemanden einsetzen
rationale: A person as direct object and saymiwole rayyəs establish political backing. Unlike round-1 iḏo idiom, no hand noun is present; one passage.

summary: New sense 11: (Gebote, Anweisungen) befolgen, einhalten
rationale: Command objects with applying love establish obedience, not physical retention. Three verses within one discourse; merge repeated proposals.

summary: New sense 12: (mit Objekt und masul) für verantwortlich halten

rationale: Object -la resumes the entire community; masul supplies collective responsibility after one member commits a crime. One attestation.

summary: New sense 13: (von Krankheiten) befallen, erfassen
rationale: Pneumonia and fever are seizing subjects with affected person/body: recurring disease-affliction meaning, not voluntary holding.

summary: example for sense 9 in Infectum (Jan 1.8/278)

data.turoyo: ṭray mənayye lə məskət aʕmayye...
data.translation: Keep away from them; do not join them ...

rationale: New association construction.

summary: example for sense 10 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.7/1867)

data.turoyo: Hayo wa, parti we, u ḥa, d məskiwole, saymiwole rayyəs.
data.translation: That was it, it was a party, and whoever they supported, they used to make him mayor.

rationale: New political backing; result clause disambiguates.

summary: example for sense 11 in Infectum (Jan 2.10/2776)

data.turoyo: ʕAl haṯe iḏa d huwena mšiḥoye, ḥaqiqi klozəm d məskina u fəqdono di ḥubo w mṭabqinala b ruḥayna.
data.translation: Therefore, if we become true Christians, we must keep the command of love and put it into practice ourselves.

rationale: New command-observance construction.

summary: example for sense 12 in Infectum (Jan 2.26/4451)

data.turoyo: Ṣəroyo d soyəm suǧ i məlle kulla kməskila masul.
data.translation: A Christian who commits a crime, they hold the whole community responsible.

rationale: Only responsibility-construction attestation.

summary: example for sense 13 in Preterit (Jan 2.4/858)

data.turoyo: Hawxa ḥəmme gawonayto kəmmila. Msəkla i lašayḏi kula.
data.translation: An internal fever like this, they call it. It seized my whole body.

rationale: Illness subject and affected body explicit.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (Jan 1.22/1150)

data.turoyo: Qayəm l babi msəkle u Malke dəb Saʕido, məb Sorino b kallat, u Malke dəb Ḥano w mšayaʕle ḥoṯi aʕmayye l Mawṣal.
data.translation: Then my father engaged Malke of the Saido family, from Sorino, for money, and Malke of the Hano family, and sent my sister with them to Mosul.

rationale: Round-1 I.2 Preterit has three examples; l-agent and payment clear.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.36/1515)

data.turoyo: Bəṯər msəkwolan wakilo. Kumarno msalmiwolan l ḥa wakilo, tre-tloṯo mi ǧamaʕayḏan, maʕ ʕlayme, hanək ḥayriwo lak kallatani.
data.translation: Afterwards we had appointed an agent. I am saying, we had entrusted them to an agent, two or three from our congregation, from the young men; those used to look after this money.

rationale: New I.2 Preterit-wa cell; wakilo already in round 1.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.16/825)

data.turoyo: I ḥkume məskowalle b ḥaq dəṯṯe
data.translation: The government had hired them for their pay;

rationale: Institutional suffix coding; thin I.2 Preterit-wa.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.22/1142)

data.turoyo: Qayəm huwwole xbariye aʕlayye, msəkiwonne šawʕo, šnəqənne, kəllən b Alʕaziz aq qawraṯṯe.
data.translation: Then he informed on them; they arrested seven of them and hanged them. Their graves are in Elazığ.

rationale: I.1 Preterit-wa has two examples before this round.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.55/2621)

data.turoyo: U ḥa d məmsakwo ʕaraq qačaġ gabe mǧazanwole.
data.translation: Whoever was caught with illicit arak in his possession, they would punish him.

rationale: Detransitive Infectum-wa has only an isolated form before Jan.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 3.15/187)

data.turoyo: Bu rabəʕ dann 1972 daʕoro mi Qaməšlo l Nṣiwən kmanṭe aʕme buyone w kṯowe d ṬDO w kməmsək bu ḥdud b Nṣiwən.
data.translation: In the spring of 1972 he is returning from Qamishli to Nusaybin, bringing TDO statements and books with him, and he is arrested at the border in Nusaybin.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell; narrative k- contrasts habitual -wa.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: einnehmen, nehmen, ergreifen, fangen; halten, festhalten, behalten
rationale: 1/53 and 29/24 already establish sustained holding and retention; PrS 8/6 and 25/52 establish grasping. Clarifies the questioned halten??? and the difference between capture and continued possession, without separating participant extensions.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək qime (mit l-) 'Wertschätzung entgegenbringen'

data.turoyo: Bi səbbe d babayna, ǧəddayna, d kətwulle əšmo kayiso bi ṣənʕa, l ayko d əzzanowo, məskiwolan qime, baq qəryawoṯo, b Məḏyaḏ, b kul dukṯo.
data.translation: Weil unser Vater und unser Großvater einen guten Ruf im Handwerk hatten, brachte man uns, wohin wir auch imer gingen, hohe Wertschätzung entgegen, in den Dörfern, in MgQ.yag, Allerorten.

rationale: Collocation with esteem noun and person indexed by -lan.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək sir 'eine Haut bekommen'

data.turoyo: gǧəmdo bas səfoqe, kməsko sir
data.translation: Er kühlt sich in den Schalen ab und bekommt eine Haut.

rationale: Single clear food-preparation attestation; product noun supplies the specific acquired layer.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək baṣro 'Fleisch ansetzen'

data.turoyo: Bəṯr məd aṯi u ḥṣodo, kmanšəfi a ʕwone, lašan d məski čike d baṣro, d howən qalaw
data.translation: Wenn die Erntezeit gekommen ist, dann melken sie die Schafe nicht mehr, damit sie etwas Fleisch ansetzen können, damit sie wohlgenährt sind

rationale: Single clear attestation: ewes gain body substance; record as collocation rather than general production sense.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək i Ndaṯalo 'an der Muttergottes und ihrem Fest festhalten'

data.headword: msəkle/mosək i Ndaṯalo 'an der Muttergottes und ihrem Fest festhalten'
data.turoyo: kətwo bu waxt d meqəm ṭabi, zlam mhayməno ġalabe. musakwo i Ndaṯalo, a tloṯo yawme di Ndaṯalo, du ʕeḏo di Ndaṯalo.
data.translation: Es gab, in früherer Zeit natürlich, einen sehr gläubigen Mann. Er hielt fest an der Muttergottes, den drei Tagen der Muttergottes, dem Fest der Muttergottes.

rationale: Single devotional observance context; the title and three feast days are appositional, so do not generalize to any festival.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək haybe (mit mən) 'Scheu, Angst vor jemandem bekommen'

data.headword: msəkle/mosək haybe (mit mən) 'Scheu, Angst vor jemandem bekommen'
data.turoyo: w msəkli haybe mene.
data.translation: Er ist mir unheimlich.

rationale: The fear noun contributes the emotion; -li indexes experiencer in the ordinary Preterit actor series.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək dost 'sich einen Liebhaber nehmen'

data.turoyo: aṯti msəklala tloṯo doṣtin, bu baž.
data.translation: und meine Frau nahm sich drei Liebhaber auf dem Festland.

rationale: Two independent contexts with coreferential additional l-suffix and lover noun; one example suffices.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək ruḥo 'sich beherrschen, an sich halten; aushalten'

data.headword: msəkle/mosək ruḥo 'sich beherrschen, an sich halten; aushalten'
data.turoyo: lə kqoḏer mosək ruḥe, ksoyəm ʕam an niše daṭ ṭaye.
data.translation: Er aber konnte sich nicht beherrschen und verführte die Weiber der Muslime.

rationale: Repeated reflexive self-control/endurance; distinguish literal maintaining balance at 29/470.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək iḏo d- 'jemandes Partei ergreifen'

data.turoyo: i ʕašərto msəkla iḏe du brazi
data.translation: Der Stamm ergriff die Partei des Neffen

rationale: The tribe supports the nephew; hand noun is not a bodily patient in this dispute.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək nawba 'Wache halten'

data.turoyo: Man ṭro mosək nawba bi qamuṯo?
data.translation: Wer soll zuerst Wache halten?

rationale: Two occurrences of the same watch-taking expression; one concise example selected.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək rišo d- 'sich an die Spitze stellen'

data.headword: msəkle/mosək rišo d- 'sich an die Spitze stellen'
data.turoyo: W gdoṯeno mosakno riša di ʕašərtayḏux stene.
data.translation: und werde kommen und mich auch an die Spitze deines Stammes stellen.

rationale: Single clear leadership collocation, related to inherited dukṯo expression but with a different noun.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək zəngoro 'Grünspan ansetzen'

data.turoyo: Čəngi meqəm ṣəfər we, u ṣəfər musakwo zəngoro, d lə mbayḏiwonne, msamamwo, quṭalwo u ʕamo.
data.translation: Because in the old days they were copper, and copper used to acquire verdigris; if they did not tin them, it would poison, it would kill the people.

rationale: New material-acquisition idiom; compare round-1 sir.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək taǧara 'ein Geschäft aufnehmen'

data.turoyo: Kul ḥa msəklele taǧara rabṯo w Məḏyaḏ yariwo w hawi b... Məḏyaḏ yariwo, ʕamiro.
data.translation: Each one took up a substantial business, and Midyat developed and became... Midyat developed, built up.

rationale: New business collocation; retain reflexive beneficiary.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək ṣənʕa 'ein Gewerbe aufnehmen'

data.turoyo: Kul ḥa msəklele ṣənʕa w hawən more d šuġlo w ʕamlo w bote.
data.translation: Each one has taken up a trade for himself, and they have become owners of businesses and work and houses.

rationale: New livelihood collocation, not employment of a worker.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək šuġlo 'Arbeit finden; einen Auftrag übernehmen'

data.headword: msəkle/mosək šuġlo 'Arbeit finden; einen Auftrag übernehmen'
data.turoyo: Azzənwo b zabno, msəkwolle šuġlone w hawənwo zangin ġalabe.
data.translation: They had gone earlier, had obtained jobs, and had become very rich.

rationale: One idiom example; government-contract variant at Jan 2.7/1863 discussed in note.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək daʕwe 'einen Rechtsfall übernehmen, bearbeiten'

data.turoyo: Ġalabe daʕawi msəkli w mḥayṣəlili w səmili kulle ṭapo ʕal əšme dam moraṯṯe.
data.translation: I took on many lawsuits and won them, and made them all into title deeds in their owners’ names.

rationale: Professional light-verb collocation with case object and legal outcome.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək b-bolo 'im Gedächtnis behalten'

data.turoyo: Zəmriwo, maʕlum yo, u mede d latyo hno, lə msəklan b bolayna.
data.translation: They would sing, of course; what is not, that, we have not held it in our minds.

rationale: New memory idiom; retain disfluent supplied English.

summary: New idiom: msəkle/mosək Yawmuno 'ein Tagebuch führen'

data.turoyo: Kbode u Xori, d mosək "Yawmuno" laʕ ʕlaqat, dawile ʕam i dawle d Tərkiya, 1957-1996 = 41 əšne.
data.translation: The Khori begins to keep a “Yawmuno” [Diary] about the relations he had with the state of Turkey, 1957–1996 = 41 years.

rationale: New written-record collocation; contact remains a question.

summary: Employment is recurrent in independent PrS, JTM and Ritter contexts. Worker NPs are unmarked; extra l-suffixes can identify beneficiaries. The -nne at JTM 1.1/89 cannot be securely identified as beneficiary rather than worker-object indexing.

Fruit-bearing has both expressed fruit objects and absolute garden predicates. The l-marked garden actor in PrS 58/12 is not an animate captor; this is lexical production, not merely an inanimate-agent extension.

Detransitive Preterit describes entry into capture with msik, msikət and msəkno; Part. Pass. describes continued captivity with durations; Infectum covers catchability and future trapping. Infinitiv action nouns must be distinguished from these Detransitive forms.
Infectum-wa has habitual, durative, wish and counterfactual contexts; ko-Preterit kəmsəkli at PrS 85/39 adds a form box. g-...-wo in PrS 83/57 needs aspectual clarification.

The inherited b-ʕaql and dukṯo expressions are already in stem notes, although the parsed idioms list is empty. They are retained without duplicate proposals. New noun combinations were searched through glossary_lookup.py; another verb sharing haybe or nawba does not duplicate an msk headword.

Several PrS citations are edition page/line numbers rather than supplied text/verse references. Near-identical passages are evidence for deduplication, not enough to rewrite the citation concordance. Only the Ritter 21/43–44 range correction is explicit.
Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. Supplied English is project machine translation, retained verbatim where quoted; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Round-1 I.2–5 and Detransitive I.1 are retained; this round starts new integer senses at 6. Reader thin-cell counts often omit round 1 and were recomputed.

Jan here includes interviews and Turkish glosses as well as written commentary and religious discourse. Learned fəqdono/waṣiye and Yawmuno belong to specific command and diary contexts; do not characterize the whole sample as uniform literary prose.

Preterit l-series capture/engagement contrasts with Detransitive məmsək. Reduced msəkwo/msəkiwo remain uncertain; the new Detransitive Preterit-wa example is provisional. Genitive-patient msoko d ḥasyo Tuma is an action Infinitiv, not Detransitive just because its agent is absent, matching round 1.
No alignment flags are supplied, but English can still mislead: Jan 2.26/4483 əzən likely means permission, not motion. No example with that mistranslation is published.
Confirm judicial amsək at PrS 77/33–34 as condemnation rather than an order of detention; both opposing bribes support the judicial interpretation.
Check JTM 2.7/10 məsakwole: does samdo bind the mixture, does the mixture cohere, or do people continue handling it? Check actor and -le reference.
Verify MAC dmašək and the scope of know/realize at Unfortunate Youth/28; physical holding of the rod remains possible.
Verify misko and Kli in PrS 80/34; no spelling normalization or new sense has been published from this alone.
Verify root and suffixes of msaḳanne at 68/52. Time-occupation meaning is not attributed to msk until then.
Confirm segmentation of msəklelan at 65/48 and the attachment of b iḏoṯayxu at 63/36.
Confirm whether JTM 4.1/2 names devotion to the Mothergottes, observance of her three feast days, or both; no generalized festival sense is claimed.
Check sir (skin/cream), qime (esteem) and beneficiary versus object indexing in JTM employment clauses. Preserve the edition translations meanwhile.
Check the PrS page/line versus text/verse concordance before changing any inherited PrS references.
Confirm əzən permission at Jan 2.26/4483 and supply a corrected translation before publishing a new permission collocation.
Confirm reduced msəkwo at Jan 1.39/1722, 3.38/1103 and msəkiwo at 2.3/287: Detransitive Preterit-wa, clipped active or Part. Pass. plus copula? New box is provisional.
Resolve suffix coding in government məskowalle at Jan 1.16/821,825 and msəkalle at 2.4/1027; distinguish agent, patient, beneficiary.
At Jan 1.8/306 is the headman selected, backed or arrested? At 2.2/153 is nošo an object of capture or an objecting subject? At 4.II/944 does mosək darəxto mean use/handle or ride?
Confirm trade continuation/takeover at Jan 2.12/3112 and lawyer case-taking versus custody at 1.53/2552; no separate senses published.
Is Yawmuno keeping comparable to Turkish günlük tutmak, and how productive is b-bolo versus inherited b-ʕaql? Contact is a question, not an asserted origin.
Correct German 'faste' to 'fasste'
rationale: In 'faste er mich am Arm' the verb is fassen; its past form is fasste (edition spelling faßte in the supplied 11/284 translation).

summary: Restore the final t in 'gesetzt'
rationale: The perfect construction requires 'ins Gefängnis gesetzt hatten', as in the supplied 21/43 translation.

summary: Correct the article in 'König des Ortes'
rationale: Ortes is masculine/neuter genitive singular; 'der Ortes' is an evident grammatical slip. The supplied 21/43 translation has 'König des Ortes'.

summary: Correct 'Königssehn' to 'Königssohn'
rationale: The compound is Königssohn. The supplied 21/64 translation reads 'der gefangene Königssohn', corresponding to abrə-d-u=malko.

summary: Correct the heading 'Idiomaric phrases'
rationale: The stem notes contain the misspelled heading 'Idiomaric phrases' immediately before the idiomatic expressions. The intended heading is Idiomatic phrases, also used elsewhere in this batch.

summary: Use accusative 'einen Platz' in the idiom gloss
rationale: The idiom gloss takes Platz as the direct object of einnehmen, requiring masculine accusative einen. Its own example translation has 'meinen Platz eingenommen'.

summary: Subjects include adhesive wax (PrS 42/47); a vessel taking treatment (JTM 1.5/12); objects include magical powers (PrS 58/29), good advice (62/257), property (63/36) and political territory (JTM 5.2/35; 24/242). These retain taking/holding and do not warrant separate senses.
Detransitive Part. Pass. may describe reciprocal gripping with b-ḥḏoḏe (PrS 18/79), extending the held state rather than literal imprisonment.
Jan corroborates round-1 hiring I.2 with guards, sweepers, escorts and agent; government suffix coding remains unresolved.
Crop yield ṭaʕno supports round-1 fruit-bearing I.3; reader I.1 is corrected, without repeating I.3.
Headman/government support corroborates the round-1 iḏo idiom; no duplicate proposal.
Hostage role graw extends the captured patient; round-1 PrS 59/34 already has captivity as graw.
Domestic rams and sheep are kept over time; sustained possession does not by itself entail breeding.
šuġlone with contract framing means undertaking government work, unlike finding employment at Jan 1.22/1118; retain this role contrast within the idiom.
Reflexive ruḥ- includes physical shielding, cautious self-maintenance and standing one’s ground. Do not equate all three with round-1 self-control.
Frontier control continues round-1 territorial holding. First msəkle at 3726 is an interrupted boundary clause, unsuitable alone.
Watercourse subject introduces containment; duration versus volume is unresolved.
Gendarmes with qumayye extend round-1 blocking-passage I.5.
Taking another partner with reflexive beneficiary parallels round-1 dost; legal marriage status is unestablished.
Reciprocal ḥḏoḏe in a social scene may mean joining; lexical gathering requires confirmation.
Capturing an utterance ʕal lišonayye extends catching to compromising speech.
